<b>1820</b>El danés Hans Christian Ørste: 1820The Dane Hans Christian Ørsted sees that a current deflects a compass needle: electricity and magnetism are related. A few weeks later, André-Marie Ampère studies the forces between currents.
<b>1821</b>Michael Faraday construye el: 1821Michael Faraday builds the first electric motor: a wire carrying current that turns around a magnet, with its ends dipped in mercury.
<b>1837</b>El estadounidense Thomas Dave: 1837The American Thomas Davenport patents one of the first electric motors with a practical use. The commutator, which reverses the current every half turn so that the motor does not stop, had been invented a few years earlier.
<b>1925</b>Chester Rice y Edward Kellogg: 1925Chester Rice and Edward Kellogg, of General Electric, publish the design of the moving-coil cone loudspeaker, which, with few changes, still sounds in every home today.

Una corriente en un campo siente una fue: A current in a field feels a force
es la fuerza sobre un hilo de longitud L: is the force on a wire of length L carrying current I perpendicular to a field B.
Dentro de un campo magnético, cada carga: Inside a magnetic field, each moving charge experiences a force perpendicular to its velocity and to the field. A current is a lot of charges moving along a wire, so the whole wire gets a push: $F = I L × B$.\n\nIf the wire is perpendicular to the field, it is $F = I L B$. Its direction is given by the right-hand rule: fingers along the current towards the field, and the thumb points along the force. If you reverse the current, the force also reverses. Loudspeakers and motors are based on this.
El altavoz: una bobina que empuja un con: The loudspeaker: a coil that pushes a cone
el cono se mueve al ritmo de la corrient: the cone moves with the rhythm of the current arriving from the amplifier.
Un altavoz tiene un imán con forma de an: A loudspeaker has a ring-shaped magnet and a central pole: between the two, in a narrow gap, the field is radial, always perpendicular to the wire. Inside the gap there is a light coil attached to the paper cone.\n\nThe amplifier current is alternating and follows the shape of the sound. When it goes one way, the force pushes the coil out; when it goes the other, in. The cone vibrates with the music and moves the air: that is sound.
Cuánta fuerza hace la bobina: How much force the coil produces
con 0,5 A en una bobina de 40 vueltas en: with 0.5 A in a 40-turn coil in a 1 T field.
Todas las vueltas de la bobina cuentan c: All the turns of the coil count as a single long wire: $L = N · 2π r = 40 · 2π · 0.0125 = ${f2(L_ALT)} "m"$. Even though the coil is small, adding up its turns gives a lot of wire inside the field.\n\nWith $B = 1 "T"$ and $I = 0.5 "A"$ we get $F = B I L = ${f2(F_ALT)} "N"$. And since F is proportional to I, the cone reproduces the signal without distorting it: twice the current, twice the push. Move the slider to see it.
El motor: dos fuerzas que hacen girar: The motor: two forces that make it turn
es el par de una bobina de 100 vueltas d: is the torque of a 100-turn 4 × 3 cm coil with 0.5 A in 0.1 T.
En un motor la bobina es una espira rect: In a motor the coil is a rectangular loop that can rotate in a field. Its two long sides carry the current in opposite directions, so they receive opposite forces: one is pushed up and the other down. They do not move the coil from its place, but they make it rotate.\n\nThe resulting torque is $τ = N I S B "sin" θ$, where θ is the angle between the normal to the coil and the field. It is maximum, $τ = ${f3(TAU_MAX)} "N·m"$, with the coil parallel to the field, and zero when it is perpendicular. Move the slider to change the angle.
El conmutador: cambiar la corriente para: The commutator: reversing the current so it does not brake
el conmutador invierte la corriente, y e: the commutator reverses the current, and the torque keeps pushing the same way.
Hay un problema: al pasar la bobina por: There is a problem: as the coil passes through the vertical, the sides swap places and the torque would start to brake it, as seen in the dotted curve, which becomes negative. The coil would oscillate instead of rotating.\n\nThe solution is the commutator, a split ring with brushes that rub against it, which reverses the current exactly at that moment.
